he said:
"Make for yourself the likeness of what you saw, and you will conquer."
And the tyrant Maxentius was drowned in the river Dunbis (Tiber?).
Then he was further confirmed in the faith, together with his wife Diocletiana, the daughter of Diocletian the pagan.
And in the third year of his reign, he renovated the building of Byzantium,
and he added four miles to it.
And he transferred the empire from Rome to this Byzantium.
And he built in it a church to Irene (Peace),
and another to the Twelve Apostles.
And he made its inhabitants free citizens.
And he pulled down the idols,
and not one of the pagans did he allow to minister {OCR?}.
And Queen Helena, his mother, went up to Jerusalem,
and investigated concerning the Cross of our Lord and found it.
And a part of it she placed in the temple which she built over the Tomb,
and the remainder she sent to the king.
And in the time of Constantine the victorious, the Iberians believed in Christ;
and they sent to the king and received bishops and priests and were baptized.
And also the Sarmatians, the Goths, and the Scythians, when the king conquered them,
believed and were baptized.
And he built a great church beside the oak of Mamre,
where Abraham received the revelation.
And also in Baalbek of Phoenicia he built a church,
because its inhabitants were in great error:
their wives were held in common,
and the father of anyone was not known.
And when he appointed for them a bishop,
little by little they were reformed.
And he built in Antioch an octagonal temple.
And he made a bridge over the river Dunbis (Danube?),
and his forces crossed over.
And he subdued the Scythians,
and brought them to the faith.
And he assembled the ecumenical council of three hundred and eighteen [bishops],
and they confirmed the faith,
in the year six hundred and seventy-seven of the Greeks.
And the canons of the fast and of Pascha were arranged by his hands.
In his days,
Shapur the king of Persia persecuted the Christians in his dominion.
And he also went up against Nisibis,
and turned back from it as Diocletian did, as this book has said on page... {OCR?}
Now Constantine had taken Minervina among his wives,
and after her death... the First Council of Nicaea... Maximianus... {OCR?}
